evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a child AC whose observable is the parent's: a test or grep demonstrating no completion-verifier module is modified to re-run world measurements (e.g. change-diff assertion over completion-verifier paths), so parent AC-4 is covered in the same terms rather than by a plan-review-module grep.
evidence: Parent AC-4: 'the completion-verifier is NOT made to re-run world measurements — the rejected alternative stays rejected, and a test or grep demonstrates it'.

Child f161 AC-9: 'the rejected alternative stays rejected ... grep -rnE ... src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py prints nothing (exit 1), i.e. the module is a pure-stdlib text check with no network or shell reach'.

search_files on det_measurement_provenance.py for 'completion' returns no matches — the grepped module is unrelated to the completion-verifier, so AC-9 measures a different subject than parent AC-4 names.
Three-part standard: SAME OBSERVABLE fails (parent=completion-verifier untouched; child=new plan-review module has no network reach); measured IN THE SAME TERMS fails.

Corroboration: the epic-close comment had to reconstruct AC-4 by enumerating change 1423's diff and asserting 'No completion-verifier module is modified ... a negative AC is otherwise unfalsifiable' — an ad-hoc proof the child AC-9 grep did not supply.
findings.finding: Parent AC-4 names the COMPLETION-VERIFIER as the thing that must not be made to re-run world measurements ('the completion-verifier is NOT made to re-run world measurements ... a test or grep demonstrates it'), but the only child AC addressing the rejected alternative (child f161 AC-9) greps src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py — a PLAN-REVIEW module — to prove IT has no network/shell reach. No child AC produces the parent's stated observable (a test or grep demonstrating the completion-verifier is not modified to re-run world measurements). The child's proof is a related but different observable, so the parent criterion is only PARTIALLY covered.
scenarios: Completion-verifier: a future change adds world-measurement re-run logic to a completion-verifier module; child f161 AC-9's grep (scoped to det_measurement_provenance.py) would still pass green, so the parent's rejected alternative is not actually guarded by any child AC in its own terms.
Completion verifier of THIS epic: reconciling AC-4 requires a proof the child does not carry, forcing manual diff-enumeration at close time (as the close comment shows).
findings.suggested_fix: In child f161 (or a dedicated child), add an AC that pins the completion-verifier as the subject — e.g. a diff/grep assertion that no completion-verifier module (workflow_ops / completion verifier package) gains world-measurement re-run code — so the child's observable matches parent AC-4 exactly, instead of only proving the new plan-review DET module is pure-stdlib.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one sentence to the Approach (or ADR-0061) acknowledging established provenance/attestation vocabularies (e.g. W3C PROV, in-toto/SLSA predicates) and stating why a purpose-built human-writable four-field line is chosen over aligning to them.
evidence: Plan: 'Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields — environment, principal, and privilege posture relative to production.'
ADR-0061 defines the four keys and enum sets as a new inline text contract with no reference to any external provenance model.

Retrieved prior art: W3C PROV models provenance as entities/activities/agents; in-toto/SLSA attestation predicates and Chainloop's evidence store are established frameworks for associating provenance metadata with artifacts/evidence (jfrog.com/learn/grc/software-attestation, legitsecurity SLSA series, github.com/chainloop-dev/chainloop).

ANTI-FP note: the underlying MECHANISM (a det_*.py leaf mirroring det_operator_attested.py surfaced via advisory p6_ac_quality) is a well-trodden internal pattern — this is a schema-shape prior-art nudge, not a novel-architecture finding.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a bespoke measurement-provenance schema (a four-field 'provenance:' continuation line: environment/principal/privilege_posture/instrument) without noting whether any established evidence/attestation-provenance vocabulary was considered as a shape to align to or deliberately diverge from.
findings.location: Approach step 1 ('Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields') and ADR-0061 Decision section
scenarios: A future promotion (98df) or a downstream rebar client wants provenance data to be machine-consumable or interoperable, and discovers the bespoke line-format diverges gratuitously from established attestation predicates.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 1 or ADR-0061's Decision section, note that in-toto/SLSA attestation predicates and W3C PROV were considered and a bespoke inline line was chosen deliberately because the artifact is a human-authored plan-text AC (not a machine-signed artifact), so a heavyweight predicate would be over-engineering — while keeping the field names (environment/principal/instrument) loosely PROV-aligned for future interop.

findings.finding: Approach step 3 introduces an LLM criterion that judges the provenance *declaration* against repo facts (catching 'plan attests account X, IaC names account Y'), but no acceptance criterion verifies this contradiction-detection behavior. AC1 binds the wrong-account regression fixture to the DETERMINISTIC presence check, yet a presence check only proves fields are non-empty — it cannot detect a provenance block that is present but names the wrong account (579718921998 vs 896586841071). The escape that motivates the epic is a present-but-wrong declaration, which is the LLM criterion's job, leaving that deliverable without a covering criterion.
findings.location: Approach step 3 vs Acceptance Criteria AC1/AC2

findings.finding: Parent AC1's second conjunct — 'the wrong-account escape is reproduced as a REGRESSION FIXTURE from the real 579718921998 vs 896586841071 case' — is not delivered by any roster child; it is descoped into idea 98df, which is not a covering sibling and explicitly does not claim it done. The escape is only DETECTED by the AGENT environment-contradiction rule (a), whose runtime behaviour the child moves out.
findings.suggested_fix: Split parent AC1 into two AC — (i) the DET no-LLM presence flag (delivered by f161) and (ii) the wrong-account contradiction regression fixture (delivered by 98df) — and cite 98df as the covering child for (ii); or restore the environment-contradiction regression test to f161's In-scope/Testing as an offline fixture rather than a live semantic run.
